## Define the functions 
```{r function}
#' function to make a barplot with swarm points given a fitted linear model
#' 
#' @params dt data.table with data
#' @params emm data.table with estimated marginal means from emmeans 
#' @params x string, x column data tables specifying group
#' @params y string, y column for dt only, emm depends on fixed emmeans values  
#' @params col string, grouping column
#' @params titl string, plot title
#' @params pal vector, list of color palette values for scale_color_manual
#' 
#' @return ggplot object
bar_swarm <- function(dt, emm, x, y, col, titl, 
                      pal = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal("Dark2", n = 7)) {
  # Convert emmeans to data.frame if needed
  if("emmGrid" %in% class(emm)) {
    emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm)
  } else {
    emm_df <- emm
  }

  p <- ggplot(dt, aes(x = .data[[x]], y = .data[[y]], color = .data[[col]], fill = .data[[col]])) +
   geom_col(
      data = emm_df,
      aes(x = .data[[x]], y = emmean, fill = .data[[x]]),
      width = 0.6
    ) +
    # Error bars using emmean ± SE
    geom_errorbar(
      data = emm_df,
      aes(x = .data[[x]], ymin = emmean - SE, ymax = emmean + SE, color = .data[[x]]),
      width = 0.3,
      size = 0.8,
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      color = "black"
    ) +
    geom_jitter(
      data = dt,
      aes(x = .data[[x]], y = .data[[y]]),
      position = position_jitter(width = 0.2, seed = 123), 
      size = 2,
      color = "black"
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    ggtitle(titl) +
    scale_color_manual(values = pal) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 45, 
        hjust = 1, 
        vjust = 1, 
        family = 'Arial',
        face = 'bold',
        size = 12
      ),
      axis.text.y = element_text(
        family = 'Arial',
        face = 'bold',
        size = 8
      ),
      axis.title.y = element_text(
        face = 'bold', 
        family = 'Arial', 
        size = 12
      ), 
      plot.title = element_text(
        hjust = 0.5, 
        face = 'bold', 
        family = 'Arial', 
        size = 12
      ), 
      plot.subtitle = element_text(
        hjust = 0.5, 
        face = 'bold', 
        family = 'Arial', 
        size = 8
      ),
      legend.position = 'none',
      axis.title.x = element_blank()
    )
  # # Add conditional ordering
  # if(x == "group") {
  #   p <- p + scale_x_discrete(
  #     limits = c('CM', 'Wt', 'Wt_C31', 'PS19', 'PS19_C31'),
  #     labels = function(x) gsub("_", " + ", x)
  #   )
  # }
  return(p)
}


#' Create a Compact Summary String of a Linear Model
#'
#' This function extracts key statistics from a linear model summary and formats 
#' them into a compact string suitable for plot subtitles or inline reporting.
#' The string includes R-squared, F-statistic with degrees of freedom, and p-value.
#'
#' @param model An object of class 'lm' (linear model)
#' @param digits Integer indicating the number of decimal places for R-squared and F-statistic (default: 3)
#' @param p_digits Integer indicating the number of decimal places for p-value (default: 3)
#' @param include_adj_r logical; whether to include adjusted R-squared (default: FALSE)
#'
#' @return A character string containing formatted model statistics
#'
#' @examples
#' # Create a simple linear model
#' model <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
#' 
#' # Get compact summary string
#' model_subtitle(model)
#' 
#' # Use in a ggplot
#' library(ggplot2)
#' ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
#'   geom_point() +
#'   geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
#'   labs(subtitle = model_subtitle(model, include_adj_r = TRUE))
#'
#' @export
model_subtitle <- function(model, digits = 3, p_digits = 3, include_adj_r = FALSE) {
  # Check input
  if (!inherits(model, "lm")) {
    stop("Input must be a linear model object of class 'lm'")
  }

  # Extract model summary
  s <- summary(model)

  # Extract components
  r_squared <- round(s$r.squared, digits)
  f_stat <- round(s$fstatistic["value"], digits)
  df1 <- s$fstatistic["numdf"]
  df2 <- s$fstatistic["dendf"]
  p_value <- pf(s$fstatistic["value"], df1, df2, lower.tail = FALSE)

  # Format p-value
  if (p_value < 2e-16) {
    p_str <- "p < 2e-16"
  } else if (p_value < 10^(-p_digits)) {
    p_str <- paste("p =", formatC(p_value, format = "e", digits = 2))
  } else {
    p_str <- paste("p =", round(p_value, p_digits))
  }

  # Build the result string
  if (include_adj_r) {
    adj_r_squared <- round(s$adj.r.squared, digits)
    result <- sprintf("R² = %s (adj. R² = %s), F(%d, %d) = %s, %s", 
                     r_squared, adj_r_squared, df1, df2, f_stat, p_str)
  } else {
    result <- sprintf("R² = %s, F(%d, %d) = %s, %s", 
                     r_squared, df1, df2, f_stat, p_str)
  }

  return(result)
}


#' Generalized linear model based on a flexible formula
#'
#' @param dat Data.table with the original data
#' @param m0 lmerMod baseline model with without the exposure element
#' @param outcome String specifying the column in dat containing the outcome variable
#' @param exposure String specifying the column in dat containing the exposure variable
#' @param covs Vector of column names containing covariates to be included in the formula
#' @param mat dsCMatrix a Generalized relatedness matrix
#'
#' @returns A list: 'Estimate' (beta), 'Std. Error' (se), 't value' (test statistic), 'Pr(>Chisq)' (p-value), 'nobs' (number of observations)
get_linreg <- function(dat, outcome, exposure, covs = c(), mat) {
  m <- relmatLmer( # remember in the formula, exposure must come first after ~
    as.formula(paste(outcome, "~", paste(c(exposure, covs, "(1|PIDN)"), collapse = " + "))),
    data = dat,
    relmat = list(PIDN = mat)
  )
  t <- suppressWarnings(anova(m0, m))
  a <- summary(m)
  return(as.list(c(a$coefficients[2, ], t$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2], nobs = nobs(m))))
}

#' Recodes dummy categorical variables and can subset by vector of categories
#'
#' @param dat Data.table with the original data
#' @param dcol String representing the column to be split
#' @param keep Vector of strings that are the categories within dcol to extract. default is all c()
#'
#' @returns modified data.table with new dummy variable columns named "dcol.category" after original column
recode_dummies <- function(dat, dcol, keep = c()) {
  dt <- dat
  # check input
  if (length(keep) == 0) {
    inds <- unique(dt[[dcol]])
  } else if (length(keep) > 0 & all(keep %in% unique(dt[[dcol]]))) {
    inds <- unique(dt[[dcol]])[unique(dt[[dcol]]) %in% keep]
  } else {
    stop("Keep must be a vector of names in the original column")
  }
  # split out dummies
  dt[, c(paste(dcol, inds, sep = ".")) := lapply(inds, function(x) ifelse(get(dcol) == x, 1, 0))]
  # reorder behind original variable
  v <- grep(paste0("^", dcol, "$"), names(dt))[1]
  inds <- paste(dcol, inds, sep = ".")
  setcolorder(dt, c(names(dt)[1:v], inds, names(dt)[(v + 1):(ncol(dt) - length(inds))]))
  return(dt)
}



#' Plot Heatmap with Significance Borders
#'
#' Creates a heatmap with significance indicators shown as borders around tiles.
#' Supports optional transposition of the heatmap axes.
#'
#' @param dt A data.table containing the data to plot
#' @param row_var Character string specifying the column to use for rows
#' @param col_var Character string specifying the column to use for columns
#' @param value_var Character string specifying the column containing values to plot
#' @param pval_var Character string specifying the column containing p-values
#' @param padj_var Character string specifying the column containing adjusted p-values
#' @param nobs_var Character string specifying the column containing sample sizes
#' @param pval_thresh Numeric threshold for p-value significance (default: 0.05)
#' @param padj_thresh Numeric threshold for adjusted p-value significance (default: 0.05)
#' @param midpoint Numeric midpoint for color scale (default: 0)
#' @param low_color Color for low values (default: "blue")
#' @param mid_color Color for midpoint values (default: "white")
#' @param high_color Color for high values (default: "red")
#' @param row_order Optional vector specifying the order of rows
#' @param col_order Optional vector specifying the order of columns
#' @param transpose Logical indicating whether to transpose the heatmap (default: FALSE).
#'   When TRUE, row_var and col_var are swapped, module terms appear on top at 45°,
#'   and nobs appear on the right axis without rotation.
#'
#' @return A ggplot2 object
#'
#' @details
#' Significance is indicated by tile borders:
#' \itemize{
#'   \item Black border: Significant by adjusted p-value (padj < padj_thresh)
#'   \item Gray border: Significant by nominal p-value (pval < pval_thresh)
#'   \item No border: Not significant
#' }
#'
#' When transpose = TRUE, the axes are swapped and formatting is adjusted so that
#' module terms appear on top at 45° angles and sample sizes appear on the right
#' axis without rotation.
#'
#' @importFrom ggplot2 ggplot aes geom_tile scale_fill_gradient2 scale_x_discrete 
#'   scale_y_discrete theme_minimal theme element_text element_blank labs margin 
#'   dup_axis sec_axis
#' @importFrom data.table copy
#' @export
plot_heatmap_with_sig <- function(dt, 
                                   row_var = "ix", 
                                   col_var = "dx", 
                                   value_var = "beta",
                                   pval_var = "pval",
                                   padj_var = "padj",
                                   nobs_var = "nobs",
                                   pval_thresh = 0.05,
                                   padj_thresh = 0.05,
                                   midpoint = 0,
                                   low_color = "blue",
                                   mid_color = "white",
                                   high_color = "red",
                                   row_order = NULL,
                                   col_order = NULL,
                                   transpose = FALSE) {
  
  # Handle transposition by swapping variables and orders
  if (transpose) {
    # Swap row and column variables
    temp_var <- row_var
    row_var <- col_var
    col_var <- temp_var
    
    # Swap ordering vectors
    temp_order <- row_order
    row_order <- col_order
    col_order <- temp_order
  }
  
  # Create significance indicators
  dt_plot <- copy(dt)
  dt_plot[, sig_type := fcase(
    get(padj_var) < padj_thresh, "padj",
    get(pval_var) < pval_thresh, "pval",
    default = "ns"
  )]
  
  # Apply row ordering
  if (!is.null(row_order)) {
    dt_plot[[row_var]] <- factor(dt_plot[[row_var]], levels = row_order)
  }
  
  # Apply column ordering
  if (!is.null(col_order)) {
    dt_plot[[col_var]] <- factor(dt_plot[[col_var]], levels = col_order)
  }
  
  # Get nobs per variable (column for normal, row for transposed)
  nobs_by_var <- if (transpose) row_var else col_var
  nobs_labels <- dt_plot[, .(nobs = unique(get(nobs_var))), by = c(nobs_by_var)]
  
  # Create nobs labels for secondary axis
  nobs_breaks <- if (transpose) {
    if (!is.null(row_order)) row_order else unique(dt_plot[[row_var]])
  } else {
    if (!is.null(col_order)) col_order else unique(dt_plot[[col_var]])
  }
  
  nobs_labels_vec <- sapply(nobs_breaks, function(x) {
    n <- nobs_labels[get(nobs_by_var) == x, nobs]
    paste0("n=", n)
  })
  
  # Create the base heatmap
  p <- ggplot(dt_plot, aes(x = .data[[col_var]], y = .data[[row_var]])) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = .data[[value_var]]), color = "gray90") +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = low_color,
      mid = mid_color,
      high = high_color,
      midpoint = midpoint,
      name = value_var
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    ) +
    labs(x = col_var, y = row_var)
  
  # Configure axes based on transpose setting
  if (transpose) {
    # Transposed: module terms on top at 45°, nobs on right without rotation
    p <- p +
      scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE, position = "top") +
      scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE, position = "left",
                       sec.axis = dup_axis(labels = nobs_labels_vec, name = NULL)) +
      theme(
        axis.text.x.top = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 0, vjust = 0),
        axis.text.y.right = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0),
        axis.title.x.top = element_text(margin = margin(b = 10)),
        axis.title.y.right = element_blank()
      )
  } else {
    # Normal: dx on top at 45°, nobs on bottom at 45°
    p <- p +
      scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE, position = "top", 
                       sec.axis = dup_axis(labels = nobs_labels_vec, name = NULL)) +
      scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
      theme(
        axis.text.x.top = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 0, vjust = 0),
        axis.text.x.bottom = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
        axis.title.x.top = element_text(margin = margin(b = 10))
      )
  }
  
  # Add borders for pval significance (gray)
  if (any(dt_plot$sig_type == "pval")) {
    p <- p + geom_tile(
      data = dt_plot[sig_type == "pval"],
      aes(x = .data[[col_var]], y = .data[[row_var]]),
      fill = NA,
      color = "gray50",
      linewidth = 0.8
    )
  }
  
  # Add borders for padj significance (black)
  if (any(dt_plot$sig_type == "padj")) {
    p <- p + geom_tile(
      data = dt_plot[sig_type == "padj"],
      aes(x = .data[[col_var]], y = .data[[row_var]]),
      fill = NA,
      color = "black",
      linewidth = 0.8
    )
  }
  
  return(p)
}


#' Combine Linear Regression Results
#'
#' This function reads linear regression GLM results for specified tests,
#' combines them into a single data.table, calculates FDR-adjusted p-values by
#' diagnosis group, and merges with module term information.
#'
#' @param input Character string specifying the base directory path where 
#'   test subdirectories are located.
#' @param cogs Character vector of test names (e.g., c("ADNI_MEM", "ADNI_EF")).
#'   Each name should correspond to a subdirectory in the input path.
#' @param sum_dt A data.table containing module information with required columns:
#'   \itemize{
#'     \item module: Module identifier (matches 'ix' in result files)
#'     \item term: Module term/description
#'   }
#' @param is.pred Logical of whether or not the data is predicted values, and
#'   the module names are appended with ".pred". Will be removed for merging 
#'   with sum_dt. Default is FALSE
#'
#' @return A data.table with combined results containing:
#'   \itemize{
#'     \item All columns from the original regression files
#'     \item stat: Renamed from either 'z stat' or 't stat'
#'     \item padj: FDR-adjusted p-values (calculated within each dx group)
#'     \item LogP: -log10 transformed p-values
#'     \item term: Module term merged from sum_dt
#'   }
#'
#' @details 
#' The function searches for files matching the pattern "GNPC.*\\.{cog}\\.linreg_glm\\.csv\\.gz"
#' in subdirectories named after each test. It handles multiple or missing
#' files with warnings. The statistical column is standardized to 'stat' regardless
#' of whether it was originally 'z stat' or 't stat'.
#'
#' @importFrom data.table fread setnames rbindlist
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{
#' # Read results for memory and executive function tests
#' results <- combine_glm_results(
#'   input = "/path/to/results",
#'   cogs = c("ADNI_MEM", "ADNI_EF"),
#'   sum_dt = module_terms
#' )
#' }
combine_glm_results <- function(input, cogs, sum_dt, is.pred = FALSE) {
  
  # Read individual cognitive test results
  dat <- lapply(cogs, function(i) {
    # List files matching the pattern
    pattern <- paste0("dataProt_SS-205063.*\\.", i, "\\.lme4qtl\\.csv\\.gz$")
    file_path <- list.files(
      path = file.path(proj.dir, input, i),
      pattern = pattern,
      full.names = TRUE
    )
    
    # Read the file (assuming one match per directory)
    if (length(file_path) == 1) {
      fread(file_path)
    } else if (length(file_path) > 1) {
      warning(paste("Multiple files found for", i, "- reading first match"))
      fread(file_path[1])
    } else {
      warning(paste("No file found for", i))
      return(NULL)
    }
  })
  
  # Standardize column names (z stat or t stat -> stat)
  dat <- lapply(dat, setnames, 
    old = c("z stat", "t stat"), 
    new = c("stat", "stat"),
    skip_absent = TRUE
  )
  
  # Combine all results
  dat <- rbindlist(dat, fill = TRUE)
  
  # Calculate FDR-adjusted p-values by diagnosis group
  dat[, padj := p.adjust(pval, method = "fdr"), by = dx]
  
  # Add -log10 transformed p-values
  dat[, LogP := -log10(pval)]
  
  # remove .pred suffix
  if (is.pred) dat[, ix := gsub(".pred", "", ix)]
  
  # Merge with module terms
  dat <- merge(dat, sum_dt[, .(module, term)], by.x = "ix", by.y = "module")
  
  return(dat)
}


```

```{r make_seurat, include=FALSE}
# module preservation data
gnpc <- fread("gnpc/validation/ADRCvsGNPC.preservation_summary.csv")
gnpc[, Biomarker := tstrsplit(module, "\\.", keep = 1)]
```

# Heatmap of WSS clin associations
## cog type
```{r wss_clin}
input <- "WSS_clin"
cogs <- c("Diagnosis_bin", "last_diag_bin", "MoCA", "last_MoCA")

# module preservation data
gnpc <- fread("gnpc/validation/ADRCvsGNPC.preservation_summary.csv")
gnpc[, Biomarker := tstrsplit(module, "\\.", keep = 1)]
gnpc[, Biomarker := factor(Biomarker, 
  levels = c("Merged", "PlasmaAB140P", "PlasmaAB142P", "PlasmaGFAP", 
             "PlasmaNfL", "PlasmaPTau181", "PlasmapTau217")
)]

# read in data
dat <- combine_glm_results(input, cogs, gnpc)

# plot
p <- plot_heatmap_with_sig(
  dt = dat,
  row_var = "term",
  col_var = "dx",
  value_var = "LogP",
  row_order = rev(gnpc[mean.Zsum > 2 & (is.mod + is.str >= 7), term]),
  col_order = cogs
)

ggsave( 
  filename = file.path("manuscript", "Figure_4",
    paste(nameset, "Cognitive_associations.ADRC.pdf", sep = ".")
  ),
  plot = p,
  device = cairo_pdf,
  width = 5.5,
  height = 10
)


```

```{r plotPredvalidation}
    aes(label = term),
    size = 2.5,
    max.overlaps = 25,
    box.padding = 0.3,
    point.padding = 0.3,
    max.iter = 100000,
    segment.color = "grey50",
    segment.size = 0.3
  ) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(
    title = "Module score prediction performance on hold out set",
    subtitle = "Joinet multivariate elastic net, n = 259",
    x = "Model fit (R²)",
    y = "Concordance-index",
    color = "Biomarker Type"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )

ggsave(final_plot, 
  filename = file.path("manuscript", "Figure_6", 
    paste(nameset, "prediction_performance.pdf", sep = ".")
  ),
  width = 5,
  height = 5
)
print(final_plot)

```



## compare cognitive metric associations
```{r compare_predict}
# setup vars
# cogs <- c("Diagnosis_bin", "last_diag_bin", "MoCA", "last_MoCA")
cogs <- c("MoCA", "Diagnosis_bin")
test <- c("WSS_clin", "WSS_clin_actual", "WSS_clin_predict")
names <- c("Baseline", "Follow-up Actual", "Follow-up Predicted")

# grab files
res <- rbindlist(lapply(cogs, function(j) {
  fh <- lapply(test, function(i){
    list.files(
      path = file.path(i, j), 
      pattern = paste0("*", j, ".lme4qtl.csv.gz"),
      full.names = TRUE
    )
  })
  x <- lapply(fh, fread)
  setattr(x, 'names', names)
  x <- rbindlist(x, idcol = "cohort")
  x[, ix := gsub(".pred", "", ix)]
  setnames(x, 
    old = c("z stat", "t stat"), 
    new = c("stat", "stat"), 
    skip_absent = TRUE
  )
}), fill = TRUE)


# filter to the validation set
fwrite(res, 
  file = file.path("manuscript", "Figure_6", 
    paste(nameset, "Cognitive_associations.big_tbl.csv", sep = "."))
)
res <- res[ix %in% plot_data[R2 > 0.25 & C.index > 0.65, outcome]]

plot_linreg_corr <- function(res, cog, stat = 'stat') {
  # build matrices
  mat <- as.matrix(dcast(res, ix ~ cohort, value.var = stat), rownames = "ix")
  M <- cor(mat, method = "pearson", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  P <- cor.mtest(mat, method = "pearson")
  
  # Replace upper triangle of M with p-values
  M_display <- M
  M_display[lower.tri(M_display)] <- P$p[lower.tri(P$p)]
  
  corrplot.mixed(M_display, 
    lower = 'number',
    upper = 'square',
    upper.col = COL2('BrBG'),
    lower.col = "black",
    tl.pos = "lt",
    tl.col = "black", 
    # number.cex = 0.7,
    addCoef.col = "black",
    number.digits = 3,
    title = paste(cog, "across cohorts"),
    mar = c(0, 0, 3, 0)
  )
}
# lapply(cogs, function(i) plot_linreg_corr(res[dx == i], i, stat = 'stat'))

CairoPDF(
  file = file.path("manuscript", "Figure_6",
    paste(nameset, "Cognitive_associations.corrplots.pdf", sep = ".")),
  width = 6,
  height = 12
)
par(mfrow = c(2, 1))
lapply(cogs, function(i) plot_linreg_corr(res[dx == i], i, stat = 'stat'))
dev.off()



```
